record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Give a constructive solution of spin-glass models such as the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, including a correct notion of states and an understanding of the ultrametric structure conjectured by physicists.

evidence.quote: To “solve” in a constructive sense models like the Sherrington-Kirckpatrik model is certainly an ambitious goal for the future. One should understand the correct notion of states for the model (in particular in connexion with the ultrametric structure conjectured by the physicists).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick spin-glass model defined as follows. For each integer N ≥ 1, let σ = (σ_1,…,σ_N) ∈ {−1,+1}^N denote a spin configuration, and let (g_{ij})_{1≤i<j≤N} be independent standard Gaussian random variables. At inverse temperature β > 0 and external field h ∈ ℝ, the Hamiltonian is

  H_N(σ) = (β/√N) ∑_{1≤i<j≤N} g_{ij} σ_i σ_j + h ∑_{i=1}^N σ_i,

with associated Gibbs measure G_N(σ) ∝ exp(H_N(σ)) on {−1,+1}^N.

Give a constructive solution of this model. Concretely:

(a) Define and rigorously construct a notion of "pure states" for the model in the thermodynamic limit N → ∞, providing a decomposition of the limiting Gibbs measure into extremal components.

(b) Prove, starting from the finite-volume model itself (rather than from auxiliary identities or assumed structural properties of asymptotic Gibbs measures), that the joint distribution of the overlaps R_{ℓ,ℓ'} = (1/N) ∑_{i=1}^N σ^ℓ_i σ^{ℓ'}_i of independent replicas (σ^ℓ)_{ℓ≥1} drawn from G_N converges, as N → ∞, to a distribution supported on ultrametric configurations:

  R_{1,2} ≥ min(R_{1,3}, R_{2,3})   almost surely,

and identify this limiting law with the hierarchical (Parisi) structure predicted by the replica-symmetry-breaking ansatz.

(c) Tie (a) and (b) together by exhibiting the ultrametric tree of overlaps as the genealogy of the pure-state decomposition constructed in (a).
artifact.status_search_result: Major progress has occurred: Talagrand proved the Parisi formula for the free energy of the SK model, and Panchenko proved the Parisi ultrametricity conjecture for asymptotic Gibbs measures satisfying the Ghirlanda–Guerra identities, which apply to the SK model. However, a fully constructive solution — including an intrinsic, model-based construction of pure states and the ultrametric tree directly from the finite-volume Gibbs measure (rather than via abstract asymptotic measures and structural identities) — is generally still regarded as incomplete. Recent work (e.g., 2025 papers on pure states of the RSB ansatz) continues to address these foundational issues.

status_evidence.title: The Parisi ultrametricity conjecture - Annals of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Panchenko proves the ultrametricity of the overlap distribution for asymptotic Gibbs measures satisfying the Ghirlanda–Guerra identities, applicable to the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model.
status_evidence.claim: Ultrametricity of the overlap distribution has been proven for the SK model in the asymptotic-Gibbs-measure framework.

status_evidence.title: On the Pure States of the Replica Symmetry Breaking ansatz
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper (2025) addressing the pure-state decomposition for the RSB ansatz in spin glasses.
status_evidence.claim: The notion of pure states for SK-type models remains an active topic of research.

status_evidence.title: The Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model - Panchenko
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph presenting the proof of the Parisi formula and ultrametricity, but framed via asymptotic Gibbs measures.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results approach ultrametricity through asymptotic Gibbs measures rather than a fully constructive finite-volume route.
